title: Lasers; Radioactive decay: types and properties
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: N02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; N02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; N02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; N02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N02-1#N.5, N02-1#N.8a, N02-1#N.10a, N02-1#N.12, N02-1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Beta-minus particle
items.clue: A fast electron emitted from the nucleus, charge –e.

items.label: Alpha particle
items.clue: A helium-4 nucleus: 2 protons and 2 neutrons, charge +2e.

items.label: Gamma ray
items.clue: A high-energy photon with no charge and no mass, emitted by a nucleus.

items.label: Nucleon number
items.clue: Top figure on each symbol in a decay equation; its total is the same on both sides.

questions.stem: A nucleus has nucleon number A and proton number Z. It undergoes an alpha decay, and the nucleus formed then undergoes a beta-minus decay. Which expression gives the number of neutrons in the final nucleus?
Sodium-22 (²²₁₁Na) decays by β⁺ emission. The daughter nucleus is left in an excited state and then emits a γ photon. What is the final nucleus?
questions.explanation: β⁺: a proton becomes a neutron, so Z falls from 11 to 10 (neon) and A stays 22. The γ photon carries away energy only: A and Z do not change.

questions.stem: A steel works checks the thickness of steel sheet, about 5 mm thick, with a radioactive source on one side of the sheet and a detector on the other. Which type of source is most suitable, and why?

options.text: α, as it is the most strongly ionising, so the steel absorbs it strongly.
β⁻, as β⁻ is partly absorbed by thin sheets, as in gauging paper.
γ, as only γ passes through 5 mm of steel, partly absorbed.
α, as its range of a few cm is greater than the 5 mm thickness of the sheet.

questions.explanation: The source must be partly absorbed: some must reach the detector, and the count must fall as the sheet thickens. Only γ does both for 5 mm of steel.

questions.stem: Predict first. With no radioactive source near it, a detector still records a count rate. Which statement about this background count rate is correct?

options.text: It is the same in every minute, so a single one-minute reading gives its value exactly and no repeat readings are needed.
It is radiation that has soaked into the detector from sources used earlier, and it fades once the detector is left unused.
It comes from cosmic rays and from radioactive nuclides in rock, air and buildings and is subtracted from each reading.
It needs to be subtracted only from the first reading taken with a source; later readings then show the source alone.

questions.stem: Thorium-232 (²³²₉₀Th) decays through a chain of α and β⁻ decays to stable lead-208 (²⁰⁸₈₂Pb). How many α decays and how many β⁻ decays are there in the chain?
